FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py:3542](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3542) and [dynamic_management.py:3577](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3577), `DynamicManager.process_round()` starts recording failures and detector state before checking whether the FSM is already terminal. The first terminal check only happens indirectly at [dynamic_management.py:3706](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3706) when `transition()` raises. I confirmed this by forcing `FAIL_CRITICAL` first, then calling `process_round({}, [], [], 1.0)`: it raised `RuntimeError` but still left `convergence_detector._round_findings == {0: []}`. That means a duplicate or late orchestrator call can corrupt round history after termination.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a hard guard at the top of `process_round()` that raises immediately if `self.fsm.is_terminal`, before any metrics, histories, or event emissions are mutated.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` computes `is_converged` and `is_diminished` at [dynamic_management.py:3580](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3580) and [dynamic_management.py:3624](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3624), then runs immune feedback at [dynamic_management.py:3636](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3636) and [dynamic_management.py:3673](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3673), where `apply_diagnosis()` can lower `tau_vocab_growth` or `tau_sim` at [dynamic_management.py:3992](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3992) and [dynamic_management.py:4005](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4005). But the FSM still receives the old booleans at [dynamic_management.py:3700](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3700). So the manager can terminate on a stop/convergence decision it has just adjusted away. The clearest case is “premature vocab saturation”: the threshold is relaxed, but `is_diminished` is not recomputed before the terminal event is chosen.  
PROPOSED_FIX: After any diagnosis that changes a current-round stop/convergence parameter, invalidate affected caches and recompute `kappa`, `converged`, and/or `stop` before calling `select_event`; or explicitly defer all such adaptations to the next round and document that policy.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `select_event()` claims to return the highest-priority applicable event, but its `round_complete` branch ignores `valid_events()` and returns `COMPLETE` by default at [dynamic_management.py:1285](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1285). Meanwhile `valid_events()` correctly reports no events in terminal state at [dynamic_management.py:1169](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1169). I confirmed that after `FAIL_CRITICAL`, calling `select_event(False, False, False, True)` returns `sigma_complete`. That is an invalid event for a terminal FSM and breaks the method’s own contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `select_event()` raise `RuntimeError` immediately when `self.is_terminal`, and in general derive every returned event from `valid_events()` instead of hand-rolling the `round_complete` fallback.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.59  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM’s self-validation and tests encode execution paths the live system cannot legally take under default config. `validate_k1()` forces `ROUND_1 -> CONVERGED` at [dynamic_management.py:1303](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1303), and the test suite also forces `SYNTH -> CONVERGED` and `SYNTH -> DIMINISHED` at [test_dynamic_management.py:517](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/tests/test_dynamic_management.py#L517) and [test_dynamic_management.py:524](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/tests/test_dynamic_management.py#L524). But default `min_rounds_for_convergence=2` and `r_min=2` at [dynamic_management.py:123](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L123) and [dynamic_management.py:129](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L129) make those paths unreachable through the real manager predicates. I confirmed `RoundProgressionFSM.validate_k1(cfg)` returns `True` even though `ConvergenceDetector.converged(1)` is false and `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop(0)` is false under the same defaults. That gives false confidence about early-stop behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Split structural FSM tests from system-level tests. If you want raw graph tests, use a config with zero gates. If you want live-behavior tests, drive transitions through detector outputs and `select_event()` instead of direct terminal events.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.45  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig` exposes `blind_first` as if it were configurable at [dynamic_management.py:116](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L116), but `RoundProgressionFSM.__post_init__()` ignores it and always starts in `BLIND` at [dynamic_management.py:1156](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1156). I confirmed `DynamicManagementConfig(blind_first=False)` still initializes the FSM in `BLIND`. That is false configurability: callers can set a value the system silently discards.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `blind_first` entirely and hard-code the invariant, or validate that it must be `True` in `__post_init__`; only keep it if you intend to support a non-blind start and wire it through the FSM.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
